answer: A concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted vouching with slashable bonds. To join, an agent needs three established peers to endorse it, and each peer locks a copper-denominated bond behind that endorsement, all published on a shared terrace anyone can audit. Faking a thousand identities demands three thousand endorsements, so the attacker's bond outlay scales with account count while reward per account stays flat. When a gale of duplicate submissions arrives, the vouching peers are slashed first, so rational operators stop endorsing strangers. Cost per identity rises; profit does not.
